subject: Captive KMS vs Managed Auditlog: pricing & packaging tradeoffs
messages:

Cc: MedBound Procurement <procurement@medbound.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Compliance packaging question — KMS/HSM vs managed auditlog pricing

Hi Evelyn,

We're finalizing our security add-on budget and need a clearer comparison between two packaging options you mentioned on the call: (A) captive KMS/HSM seats + residency (MedBound manages keys) and (B) Redwood-managed auditlog retention + SaaS KMS integration. The procurement team wants to understand:

- Upfront vs recurring cost split for each option (implementation, seats, monthly service).
- How credits/implementation amortization are normally handled for pilots -> production.
- Any minimum commit or SLA differences (latency/geo).

Can you send a short write-up with pricing bands and recommended path for a pilot (6 months) that scales to 24 months? We're targeting a PO by end of month.

Thanks — Phil
Phil Turner
Director, Platform Security
MedBound Health

Attachment: None
From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
To: Phil Turner <phil.turner@medbound.com>

Subject: Re: Compliance packaging question — KMS/HSM vs managed auditlog pricing

Hi Phil — thanks for the clear ask. High-level summary first, then a short pricing sketch and recommended pilot path.

Summary:
- Option A (Captive KMS/HSM + Residency): higher upfront implementation + optional HSM-seat fees; predictable recurring infra/residency surcharge. Good when MedBound must control keys and certify HSM usage.
- Option B (Redwood-managed Auditlog + SaaS KMS integration): lower upfront, higher recurring (auditlog ingestion & retention); faster to pilot and cheaper to iterate.

Pricing sketch (order-of-magnitude, will formalize in SOW):
- Option A:
  - Implementation & onboarding: $60k–$120k one-time (includes HSM provisioning assistance, attestation paperwork).
  - HSM seats: $2k–$5k/seat/month (depends on vendor & required warranty).
  - Residency surcharge (per-region): $8k–$18k/month (driven by reserved GPU/infra and compliance controls).
  - Credits: we can amortize up to 50% of onboarding into credits applied over 12 months for a 24-month committed deal.

- Option B:
  - Implementation & onboarding: $15k–$35k one-time (auditlog connectors, retention config).
  - Auditlog retention: $0.XX–$0.XX per GB/month (we'll provide banding; typical mid-market is $1k–$6k/month for audit volumes below 1TB).
  - No HSM seats; integrates with your SaaS KMS (no seat license) but we support customer-managed keys for data at rest.
  - Credits: can offer pilot credits to offset onboarding (typically 25–40% for 6-month pilots tied to commit).

Pilot recommendation (MedBound): start with Option B for 6 months to validate ingestion patterns and alerting; concurrently prototype the captive KMS path for certification if required by compliance. If you need a hardened, certifiable deployment at production scale, transition to Option A at year 1 with onboarding credits to offset implementation.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben to run a detailed price-breakdown spreadsheet (attached) with bands tied to audit volume and HSM seats.
2) If procurement OK, we issue a pilot SOW (6 months) for Option B with a target credit and a PO-friendly purchase path.

I'll attach a draft SOW and price CSV for your review.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0118

Attachments: SOW_captive-kms-draft.pdf (stub), price-breakdown-medbound.csv (stub)
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Compliance packaging question — KMS/HSM vs managed auditlog pricing

Eve / team — appended are the numbers I promised. Quick notes:

- I created three volume buckets for audit logs (<=250GB/mo, 250GB–1TB/mo, >1TB/mo). Each band has a retention-tier price and an optional egress/ingest charge.
- For captive KMS we've modeled two scenarios: (1) HSM seat-based billing (annual seats) and (2) pass-through licensing + per-month ops fee. Seat scenario is more predictable for you; pass-through is lower upfront but higher variability.

On amortization/credits: recommended play is 50% onboarding credit amortized over the first 12 months if MedBound signs a 24-month committed plan. For a 6-month pilot-only PO, propose 35% credit applied as an invoice credit after pilot acceptance.

I lean toward starting Option B for the pilot — we can include a capped migration credit if you convert to Option A within 12 months (to avoid double billing for work we reused).

Ben
Director, Commercial Pricing
Redwood Inference

Quick technical guardrails to include in the SOW / pricing rationale:

- Captive KMS path typically requires an HSM attestation window (~4–8 weeks) and an ops runbook for key rotation + disaster recovery. Build those as line-items in implementation cost — procurement often misses the DR step.
- SLA differences: Option A can include a higher availability SLA for key ops, but Redwood's auditlog ingestion SLA for Option B is higher for short-term throughput (we operate larger fleet for log routing).
- Data residency: if MedBound requires EU-only residency later, we need to model cross-region egress and a second residency surcharge. Put a contingency line in the pricing for that.

Also suggest we add a paragraph about security attestations — what Redwood will provide (SOC2 Type II, audit evidence) vs what will be customer responsibility. That helps procurement decide crediting and acceptance criteria.

Karthik
Head of Product, Deployments
Redwood Inference

- Production path (if certified): Option A (Captive KMS/HSM) — typical transition cost $60k–$120k with a 50% onboarding credit amortized over 12 months if you commit 24 months. HSM seats priced separately; we can model a 6-seat example in the sheet.

Evelyn
